Safety.Nvidia.Effect: Removing it does not uninstall the NVIDIA driver, games or saves. Games and graphics apps may rebuild shaders, so the first launch afterwards can be slower or stutter briefly.
Safety.Nvidia.Why: The path is inside a known NVIDIA shader-cache directory.
Safety.Pip.Effect: Cached downloads can be fetched again. Removing this file does not uninstall installed Python packages.
Safety.Pip.Why: The path is inside pip's HTTP/download cache.
Safety.Updater.Effect: Removing an old cached installer usually only means the application must download it again for a future update.
Safety.Updater.Why: The file looks like an installer stored in a per-user updater directory, not an installed program location.
Safety.NuGet.Effect: Projects may need to restore these packages again. Avoid removing it while builds or development tools are running.
Safety.NuGet.Why: The path is inside the NuGet package store, which can be restored but may be actively used by development tools.
Safety.Temp.Effect: The file is inside a temporary-data location. An application may recreate it if needed.
Safety.Temp.Why: The path is inside a Windows or per-user temporary-data directory.
Safety.Browser.Effect: Removing cached files does not remove bookmarks or saved passwords. The browser may reload data and feel slower on the next launch.
Safety.Browser.Why: The path identifies a cache subtree inside a known Chromium-based browser profile.
Safety.AppCache.Effect: The application can often recreate cache data, but NODR does not know this application's cache semantics well enough to call it safe automatically.
Safety.AppCache.Why: The path looks like a cache directory, but the owning application's behavior is not known with enough confidence.
Safety.Android.Effect: Removing it may erase apps, settings and user data stored inside this Android virtual device. Manage or wipe the AVD through Android tooling instead.
Safety.Android.Why: The file is a disk image inside an Android Virtual Device directory.
Safety.Docker.Effect: It may contain Docker images, containers and volumes. Reclaim space through Docker instead of deleting the disk file directly.
Safety.Docker.Why: The file is a virtual-disk format and its path/name identifies Docker.
Safety.Wsl.Effect: It may contain an entire WSL distribution and its files. Removing it directly can destroy that environment.
Safety.Wsl.Why: The file is a virtual-disk format associated with WSL.
Safety.VirtualDisk.Effect: This file can contain an operating system, applications and user data for a virtual machine. Remove it only through the software that owns it.
Safety.VirtualDisk.Why: The extension is a virtual-disk format that can contain persistent data.
Safety.Database.Effect: Database files can contain persistent application or user data. Deleting one directly can cause data loss or break the application that owns it.
Safety.Database.Why: The extension is a database format commonly used for persistent data.
Safety.System.Effect: Deleting executable or system components directly can break Windows or an installed application. Uninstall or repair the owning software instead.
Safety.System.Why: The file is an executable/system component in a protected Windows context.
Safety.Archive.Effect: Removing it deletes this copy. It is usually safe only if you no longer need the archive or can download/recreate it again.
Safety.Archive.Why: The extension identifies an archive or disk image, but NODR cannot know whether you still need this copy.
Safety.Log.Effect: Removing it usually affects diagnostics only, but it can make later troubleshooting harder.
Safety.Log.Why: The extension identifies diagnostic/log data; it may still be useful for troubleshooting.
Safety.Program.Effect: Deleting files directly from an installed application's folder can break it. Use the application's uninstaller or storage controls instead.
Safety.Program.Why: The path is inside Program Files, where installed application components normally live.
Safety.Unknown.Effect: NODR cannot identify this file with enough confidence. Open its location and verify what owns it before removing it.
Safety.Unknown.Why: No high-confidence owner + role rule matched this path. NODR does not guess from the filename alone.

Safety.Obsidian.Effect: This is a downloaded Obsidian update artifact. Removing it does not uninstall Obsidian; a future update can download it again.
Safety.Obsidian.Why: The file is inside Obsidian's dedicated AppData\Local\obsidian-updater folder.
Safety.Python.Effect: Removing it does not uninstall Python packages. pip may download the packages again later.
Safety.Python.Why: The path is inside pip's package cache.
Safety.AndroidSdk.Effect: This file belongs to an installed Android emulator system image. Deleting it manually can break that SDK/AVD package; remove the system image through Android SDK Manager instead.
Safety.AndroidSdk.Why: The path is inside Android SDK's installed system-images directory.
Safety.Npm.Effect: Removing it does not uninstall Node packages. npm may download package data again later.
Safety.Npm.Why: The path is inside npm's package cache.
